fields.statement: An existing repo with built code comes into Rhiza: Nebari is imported first, by a written procedure, its work then runs on Rhiza workflows, and what the Nebari import teaches becomes rhiza import.

Nebari has its own Rhiza model: its built capabilities recorded area by area, its load-bearing decisions marked as the agent's made autonomously, PLAN.md, decisions.md, todo.md, .shipit/plans, afk.toml and .zap retired into Sources and deleted, its unbuilt work as draft change sets, and rhiza check and its specs green on Nebari's main; Rhiza holds Evidence of it.
Nebari's daemon builds and ships a Nebari change set on its own with Rhiza's workflows, the ship waiting on Nebari's deploy health check, with no afk or shipit left.
rhiza import brings an existing repo with built code into Rhiza through the built-in import workflow, shaped by what the Nebari import taught.
make check is green, rhiza check included, read commands stay within their budget, and the default test run binds no socket.

fields.quote: this will be the first import into rhiza so we may want to coordinate and help to model an import functionality
fields.quote_where: milestone-26-interview, after confirming that Nebari comes into Rhiza next
fields.statement: The import of an existing repo is Rhiza functionality, modelled and planned in Rhiza, with Nebari as the first import.

fields.quote: it's all agent written, it was done autonomously.
fields.quote_where: milestone-26-interview, answer on how much of decisions.md is the owner's
fields.statement: Nebari's docs/decisions.md holds no owner words: every entry was written by an agent, autonomously.

fields.quote: the existing tooling can all go away we'll use rhiza workflows but the shipit and afk folders have written plans that may be valuable during import, as well as zap.
fields.quote_where: milestone-26-interview, answer on what happens to afk, shipit and zap
fields.statement: Nebari's own tooling (afk, shipit, zap) goes away in favour of Rhiza workflows, and its written plans are material for the import.
Plan the import as a milestone with Nebari first: import Nebari by following a written import procedure, record every friction point, then build rhiza import from what was learned.
fields.wording: Milestone, Nebari first: import Nebari by hand with agents following a written import procedure, record every friction point, then build rhiza import from what we learned. The assistant's option, picked by the owner.

fields.statement: An import records built capabilities with statements and acceptance backed by the repo's existing tests now, and anchors them to code in a follow-up once anchors land.
fields.wording: Capabilities now, anchors later: record built capabilities with statements and acceptance (backed by existing specs); add anchors when the anchors capability lands, as a follow-up change set. The assistant's option, picked by the owner.

fields.statement: An import brings in as Decision nodes only the decisions that shape a capability or constraint, each worded as the agent's and marked as made autonomously and not confirmed by the owner; the rest are summarised in the Source of the decisions document.
fields.wording: Load-bearing ones only: import as Decision nodes only the decisions that shape a capability or constraint, each worded as the agent's and marked as made autonomously and not confirmed by the owner; the rest are summarised in the decisions.md Source. The assistant's option, picked by the owner.

fields.statement: An import retires planning documents into Sources and deletes them, and keeps reference, design-system, ops and deploy documents as working docs that capabilities link to; unbuilt planned work becomes change sets.
fields.wording: Retire planning, keep reference: retire PLAN.md, decisions.md, todo.md, .shipit/plans, afk.toml and .zap into Sources, then delete them; keep docs/reference, design-system.md, ops and deploy docs as working docs that capabilities link to; unbuilt PLAN/todo items become change sets. The assistant's option, picked by the owner.

fields.statement: All four pieces of milestone 26 are planned now: the import procedure, importing Nebari, the deploy check on ship and the rhiza import command.
fields.wording: A. Import procedure, B. Import Nebari, C. Deploy check on ship, D. rhiza import command, picked by the owner from the assistant's options (the assistant had recommended D as intent only).

fields.statement: The Nebari import is carried out autonomously by a daemon, as any accepted change set is, with builders following the import procedure and questions going to the arbiter or the owner's inbox.
fields.wording: Daemon, autonomously: queue it like any accepted change set; builders follow the import procedure; questions go to the arbiter or your inbox. The assistant's option, picked by the owner.

fields.statement: The Nebari import lives in Nebari's own model and is run by Nebari's own daemon; Rhiza's milestone tracks it by Evidence recorded in Rhiza.
fields.wording: In Nebari's own model: rhiza init in Nebari, open the import change set there, and Nebari's own daemon runs it; Rhiza's milestone tracks it with acceptance by Evidence recorded in Rhiza (Nebari's rhiza check and specs green on main). The assistant's option, picked by the owner.

fields.statement: rhiza import runs rhiza init when needed and starts a built-in import workflow whose agent steps do the judgment; the command is only the entry point.
fields.wording: Command starts an import workflow: rhiza import runs init if needed and starts a built-in import workflow: survey, record areas (foreach), decisions, Sources and retire docs, planned work as drafts, verify (rhiza check plus the repo's own tests). Judgment stays with agents; the command is the entry point. The assistant's option, picked by the owner.

fields.statement: The ship deploy check reads its health URL and timeout from per-repo daemon settings; unset means no deploy check.
fields.wording: Daemon setting: per-repo settings via rhiza daemon set (git config), for example ship.health-url and ship.deploy-timeout; unset means no deploy check. The assistant's option, picked by the owner.
